headline: Open Weightと非US Model Family
deck: open-weight deploymentと非US model familyの拡大を、ランキングではなくdeployment、reasoning、coding、tool use、service lifecycleの違いとして読む。

blocks.text: 8月のgpt-ossはopen-weight reasoning modelをself-hosted/local deploymentへ戻した。同じ半年にQwen、DeepSeek、Kimi、Mistral、GLMもcoding、reasoning、multimodal、agent/tool surfaceを高速更新した。open weightsはtraining/data disclosureと同義ではなく、Alibabaのregion/snapshot、DeepSeekのservice transition、Kimi/Mistralのliving index、GLMのvendor評価はそれぞれ別の境界として保持する。

must_cover_coverage.requirement: open weightsとtraining/data transparencyを混同しない
Alibaba Model Studioのsnapshot/regional/global availabilityをupstream release dateに統合しない
DeepSeek API service transitionとcheckpoint publicationを分離

boundary_coverage.requirement: Open weights do not imply an unrestricted data/training disclosure; openness should be described specifically in terms of weights/license and deployment.

The Model Studio page is a living deployment catalog; it mixes release, snapshot, regional availability, and later global availability entries. Architecture must not collapse those into one upstream model release date.
These dates establish DeepSeek API service transitions; upstream training/checkpoint publication dates must not be inferred when not stated.

The hash-pinned Kimi Code 'What's New' page is a living product document whose current rendered history begins much later; item chronology was cross-checked against Kimi's first-party platform blog/changelog during interactive verification.
The news index reliably establishes publication chronology and titles; detailed benchmark/license claims require item-level pages and should remain vendor-attributed if used in drafting.
Performance superlatives in the release notes are vendor claims; use only release identity, dates, stated feature scope, and clearly attributed evaluation claims.
